Messages.Author: jonrreeves
Messages.Body:
This isn't really a question so much as a humble request for official thumbs up.

There was a question posted on JOL recently about Condemnation: Mute on a primogen and the mechanic of negative votes. I've seen this question come up a few times, and the answer is straightforward. There is a fundamental property of the game that values can go negative. You can have negative stealth, negative intercept, negative hand strength, negative bleed, and of course negative votes.

In the process of answering the question, I went looking for some concise official statement about negative values, and I couldn't find one anywhere. As far as I can tell, the word "negative" only appears in the card rulings list once, in the context of Life Boon.

@Ankha if I may be so bold as to @ you on here, would you be willing to give me a "Correct" response on my statement above, or if I've said anything wrong, a clarifying comment, so we can link to this when answering the question? I realize most experienced VTES players don't have a problem with this concept, but I find it is not intuitive for new players (who are probably bringing context from other games which might not do this), and it would be extremely helpful to have this be discoverable from rulings at least. In the end I'd love to submit a ruling request on Condemnation: Mute specifically linking to this post, but I think it could be applied in a few other places where players have been confused in the past.

Many thanks!

Messages.Author: KoRneeshon
Messages.Body:
I think stealth, intercept, strength, bleed, and votes can all be negative and don't bottom out at 0.

The difference is in handling them. If you have -1 stealth action, -2 intercept minion cannot block it.

The remaining values can be treated as 0 virtually, but are never actually set to 0 just by being negative. If you have -2 votes, you just don't vote as if you had 0 votes, but the value is not bottomed out - if that vampire gains 4 votes, he now has 2, not 4. Strength and bleed follow similar pattern. You can still strike with -1 strength (and don't add blood / life to the target as a cost of healing...) and bleed for -1 (and don't add pool to the target if successful).

> LSJ wrote:
> If he's titled, then the number of votes his title
> is worth in the main referendum is reduced by one (negative values
> treated as zero).
>
groups.google.com/g/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/c/o9N6h9g7PPo/m/gd25YYlzheoJ

So if a primogen's title is worth -2 votes, the primogen has 0 votes with his title.
If that primogen plays a modifier for +2 votes, he would have 2 votes.
If he had another card stating that is title is worth +2 votes, he would be back to 1 vote (from his title) +2 votes from the modifier.

Reducing the number of votes a title is worth by X is not the same as giving a vampire a plain -X votes.

Correct.

> beslin wrote:
> -but that count how him have 0 votes,and if play for example Bewitching Oration to get +4 votes him now have 4 votes ( 0+4=4 )?
>
No, -2 + 4 = 2 votes.
>
> beslin wrote:
> that i understand how you wrote this
>
There is a difference between "The vampire gets -X votes" and "The vampire's title is worth -X votes".

In the first case, the votes can go negative.
In the second case, the title cannot be worth a negative value.

So:
Primogen with Condemnation Mute playing a Betwiching Oration has: 1 -3 + 4 = 2 votes.

Primogen with Rastacourere expressing votes in a Free States Rant and playing Betwitching Oration has: 0 +4 votes
since his title is worth 1-1-1 votes, which would be be negative, so it's worth 0 votes instead.
